## Page 301: Causales de Inadmisibilidad Relacionadas/ al Terrorismo (TRIG) - Exenciones Situacionales | USCIS
URL: https://www.uscis.gov/es/leyes-y-politicas/otros-recursos/casuales-de-inadmisibilidad-relacionadas-con-el-terrorismo-trig/causales-de-inadmisibilidad-relacionadas-al-terrorismo-trig-exenciones-situacionales
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Causales de Inadmisibilidad Relacionadas/ al Terrorismo (TRIG) - Exenciones Situacionales Los secretarios del Departamento de Estado y del Departamento de Seguridad Nacional, en consulta con el fiscal general, podrían autorizar exenciones de casuales de inadmisibilidad relacionadas con el Terrorismo (TRIG). Vea la sección 212(d)(3)(B) de la Ley de Inmigración y Nacionalidad (INA). Estas exenciones solo aplican a personas que participan o que probablemente participen después de entrar en actividades terroristas (Ver sección 212(a)(E)(B)(i)(II) de INA.A continuación encontrará más información acerca de cada una de las exenciones aprobadas hasta el momento.Funcionarios Públicos AfgasEmpleo como Funcionario Público en AfganistánEl 8 de junio de 2022, los secretarios de Seguridad Nacional y de Estado, en consulta entre sí y con el fiscal general, autorizaron una exención de ciertas causales de inadmisibilidad relacionadas con el terrorismo para ciertos solicitantes que fueron empleados como funcionarios públicos en Afganistán bajo los talibanes, específicamente, en cualquier momento desde el 27 de septiembre de 1996 hasta el 21 de diciembre de 2001, o a partir del 15 de agosto de 2021. Esta exención reemplaza un ejercicio similar de autoridad emitido el 18 de enero de 2017 y amplía el período cubierto para incluir el período a partir del 15 de agosto de 2021.Muchas personas que trabajaban en puestos de la administración pública en Afganistán antes del 27 de septiembre de 1996 continuaron haciéndolo después de esa fecha. Muchos lo hicieron bajo coacción u otras situaciones de dificultad. En otros casos, las personas utilizaron sus posiciones en capacidades humanitarias para mitigar las acciones represivas del régimen talibán, a do con gran riesgo personal. Posteriormente, algus de estos funcionarios públicos trabajaron para la Fuerza Internacional de Asistencia para la Seguridad, el gobier de Estados Unidos o el gobier afga que se estableció el 22 de diciembre de 2001, o prestaron asistencia a ellos. Algunas personas continuaron proporcionando servicios gubernamentales esenciales incluso después del colapso del gobier de Kabul el 15 de agosto de 2021. Esta exención permite discreción para abordar estos en adjudicaciones individuales y para cumplir con las obligaciones humanitarias de los Estados Unidos al tiempo que garantiza la seguridad e integridad de su sistema de inmigración.Para obtener más información sobre esta exención, consulte:Ejercicio de Autoridad de 2022 (Funcionario Público Afga)10 de agosto de 2022, Memorándum de Políticas de USCIS, Implementación y Autoridad de Exención Discrecional Bajo la Ley de Inmigración y Nacionalidad (INA) § 212(d)(3)(B)(i) para los Funcionarios Públicos AfgasAliados AfgasPersonas que participan en actividades de resistencia en la promoción de los intereses de los Estados UnidosEl 8 de junio de 2022, los secretarios de Seguridad Nacional y de Estado, en consulta entre sí y con el fiscal general, autorizaron una exención a ciertas causales de inadmisibilidad relacionadas con el terrorismo para los aliados afgas que apoyaron los intereses de Estados Unidos o participaron en el movimiento de resistencia contra los talibanes y otras organizaciones afiliadas, o contra la ocupación soviética de Afganistán.La participación del gobier de Estados Unidos en los asuntos afgas siempre ha dependido estrechamente de la participación de ciudadas afgas alineados con los objetivos del gobier de Estados Unidos en la región. Desde el momento de la resistencia a la agresión soviética, a través de la lucha contra el gobier del opresivo régimen talibán que permitió los ataques del 9/11 contra Estados Unidos, y durante los esfuerzos de los últimos 20 años para instalar un gobier estable y democrático frente a una creciente insurgencia, la política y los intereses estadounidenses han dependido de los valientes sacrificios de los ciudadas afgas comunes.Esta exención permite discreción para abordar estos problemas en adjudicaciones individuales y para cumplir con las obligaciones humanitarias de los Estados Unidos al tiempo que garantiza la seguridad e integridad de su sistema de inmigración.Para obtener más información sobre esta exención, consulte:Ejercicio de Autoridad (Los Aliados Afgas)10 de agosto de 2022, Memorándum de Políticas de USCIS, Implementación y Autoridad de Exención Discrecional Bajo la Ley de Inmigración y Nacionalidad (INA) § 212(d)(3)(B)(i) para los Aliados AfgasApoyo Significativo Bajo CoerciónSe pueden otorgar exenciones para solicitantes que provean apoyo significativo bajo coerción a organizaciones terroristas determinadas o  determinadas, que, como mínimo, requiere que el apoyo significativo haya sido requerido en respuesta a una amenaza razonablemente percibida de daño grave. Un ejemplo de apoyo significativo bajo coerción podría incluir proporcionar dinero o un servicio (como, por ejemplo, transportar combatientes y suministros) a un grupo rebelde bajo amenaza a punta de pistola para obedecer con tal demanda.Para más información acerca de la Exención por Proporcionar Apoyo Significativo a una Organización Terrorista  Designada, por favor vea:El 26 de febrero de 2007, Ejercicio de Autoridad (Apoyo Significativo Bajo Coerción-Organización Terrorista  Designada)El 24 de mayo de 2007, Memorándum de Implementación de USCIS, Procesamiento de Exención Discrecional a la Causal de Inadmisibilidad en Proporcionar Materiales de Apoyo a Ciertas Organizaciones TerroristasPara más información acerca de la Exención en Proporcionar Materiales de Apoyo a una Organización Terrorista Determinada, por favor vea:El 27 de abril de 2007, Ejercicio de Autoridad (Apoyo Significativo Bajo Coerción–Organización Terrorista Determinada)El 24 de mayo de 2007, Memorándum de Implementación de USCIS, Procesamiento de Exención Discrecional a la Causal de Inadmisibilidad por Proporcionar Apoyo Significativo a Ciertos Organizaciones TerroristasSolicitud de Fondos Bajo CoerciónEl secretario de seguridad nacional, en consulta con el secretario del Estado y el fiscal general, usaron su autoridad discrecional para determinar que, a partir del 7 de enero de 2011,  aplicará una casual de inadmisibilidad a ciertos solicitantes que, bajo coerción, solicitaron fondos o miembros a una organización terrorista.Para más información acerca de esta exención, por favor vea:El 7 de enero de 2011, Ejercicio de Autoridad (Solicitud de Fondos Bajo Coerción)El 23 de febrero de 2011, Memorándum de Implementación de USCIS, Implementación de una Nueva Exención Discrecional Bajo la Sección 212(d)(3)(B)(i) de la INA en Solicitar Fondos o Miembros Bajo CoerciónEntrenamiento Estilo Militar Bajo CoerciónEfectivo el 7 de enero de 2011, el secretario de seguridad nacional, en consulta con el secretario de estado y el fiscal general, usan su autoridad discrecional para  aplicar la casual de inadmisibilidad a ciertos solicitantes que, bajo coerción, recibieron el entrenamiento estilo militar de, o de parte, de una organización terrorista.Para más información acerca de esta exención, por favor, vea:El 7 de enero de 2011, Ejercicio de Autoridad (entrenamiento Estilo Militar Bajo Coerción)El 23 de febrero de 2011, Memorándum de Implementación de USCIS, Implementación de una Exención Nueva Bajo Sección 212(d)(3)(B)(i) de la INA por Recibir Entrenamiento Estilo Militar Bajo CoerciónDisposición Voluntaria de Cuidado MédicoA partir del 13 de octubre de 2011, el secretario de seguridad nacional, en consulta con el secretario de Estado y el fiscal general, autorizaron una exención para ciertos solicitantes que proporcionan cuidado médico a personas que el solicitante sabía, o razonablemente debe haber sabido, que cometieron o planificaron cometer una actividad terrorista, o a un miembro de una organización terrorista según describe la sección 212(a)(3)(B)(vi) de la INA. Un ejemplo de la disposición de cuidado médico podría incluir el proporcionar servicios en la capacidad de un profesional médico a miembros de una organización terrorista.Para más información acerca de esta exención, por favor vea:El 13 de octubre de 2011, Ejercicio de Autoridad (Disposición Voluntaria de Cuidado Médico)El 20 de viembre de 2011, Memorándum de Implementación de USCIS, Implementación de una Nueva Exención Discrecional Bajo la Sección 212(d)(3)(B)(i) de la INA por Provisión de Apoyo Significativo en Forma de Cuidado MédicoCiertos Solicitantes que Tienen Beneficios de Inmigración Actualmente (Exención General Limitada)El 10 de agosto de 2012, luego de una consulta con el secretario del Estado y el fiscal general, el secretario de seguridad nacional usó su autoridad discrecional para  aplicar los párrafos (iv)(IV), (iv)(V), (iv)(VI), y (i)(VIII) de la sección 212(a)(3)(B) de la INA, 8 U.S.C. § 1182(a)(3)(B), a ciertos extranjeros cualificados que tienen beneficios de inmigración actuales, excepto una visa de  inmigrante, que actualmente sean inadmisibles bajo las subsecciones aplicables de la sección 212(a)(3)(B)(i) de INA, debido a asociaciones anteriores (nivel III) con organizaciones terroristas  designadas. Específicamente, el uso de autoridad permite la exención de las siguientes actividades:Solicitar fondos u otros artículos de valor;Solicitarle a cualquier persona su membresía en dicha organización;Proporcionar apoyo significativo a la organización; oRecibir entrenamiento militar de, o de parte de, una organización terrorista cualificada bajo el nivel III.Para más información acerca de esa exención, por favor vea:17 de agosto de 2012, Ejercicio de Autoridad (Exención General Limitado)26 de septiembre de 2012, Implementación de una Nueva Exención Discrecional General Limitada bajo la Sección 212(d)(3)(B)(i) de INA para Solicitantes Cualificados con Asociaciones y Actividades Específicas con Organizaciones Terroristas Cualificadas  Designadas, o “Clasificación III.Levantamientos IraquíesEl 17 de agosto de 2012, el secretario de seguridad nacional, en consulta con el secretario del Estado y el fiscal general, usaron su autoridad discrecional para  aplicar la mayoría de las casuales de inadmisibilidad relacionadas con terrorismo a ciertos solicitantes que participaron en los levantamientos iraquíes en contra del gobier de Saddam Hussein en Irak entre el 1 de marzo y el 5 de abril de 1991.Para más información acerca de esa exención, por favor vea:7 de agosto de 2012, Ejercicio de Autoridad (Levantamientos Iraquíes)12 de viembre de 2012, Memorándum de Implementación de USCIS, Implementación de una Nueva Exención Bajo la Sección 212(d)(3)(B)(i) de la INA por Participación en Los Levantamientos IraquíesCierto Apoyo Significativo LimitadoEl 5 de febrero de 2014, los secretarios de Seguridad Nacional y de Estado, luego de una reunión con el fiscal general usaron su autoridad discrecional para  aplicar la casual de inadmisibilidad a ciertos solicitantes que proporcionaron cierto apoyo significativo limitado a organizaciones terroristas  designadas, o a un miembro de dicho tipo de organización. El 8 de junio de 2022, esta autoridad se amplió para incluir cierto apoyo material limitado a organizaciones terroristas designadas o miembros de dichas organizaciones.El apoyo significativo limitado puede incluir:Ciertas transacciones comerciales rutinarios:Ciertas transacciones comerciales rutinarias;Ciertas asistencias humanitarias rutinarias; yApoyo significativo proporcionado bajo la presión considerable que  alcanza ell nivel de coerción (“presión de sub-coerción”).Para más información acerca de esa exención, por favor vea:Ejercicio de Autoridad de 2022 (Cierto Apoyo Significado Limitado y Apoyo Significativo  Relevante para las Organizaciones Designadas)5 de febrero de 2014, Ejercicio de Autoridad (Cierto Apoyo Significado Limitado para las Organizaciones  Designadas)10 de agosto de 2022, Memorándum de Políticas de USCIS, Implementación y Autoridad de Exención Discrecional Bajo la Ley de Inmigración y Nacionalidad (INA) § 212(d)(3)(B)(i) para la Provisión de Cierto Apoyo Significativo Limitado y Apoyo Significativo  Relevante para las Organizaciones Designadas8 de mayo de 2015, Memorándum de Políticas de USCIS, Implementación de la Exención Discrecional de Autoridad bajo la Sección 212(d)(3)(B)(i) de INA para la Disposición de cierto Apoyo Significativo LimitadoApoyo Significativo  RelevanteEl 5 de febrero de 2014, los secretarios de Seguridad Nacional y de Estado, en consulta con el fiscal general, usaron su autoridad discrecional para  aplicar la casual de inadmisibilidad de apoyo significativo a solicitantes que proporcionaron apoyo  relevante a una organización terrorista  designada, o a un miembro de dicho tipo de organización. El 8 de junio de 2022, esta autoridad se extendió, con limitaciones adicionales, a los solicitantes que proporcionaron apoyo material insignificante a organizaciones terroristas designadas o a un miembro de dicha organización.Para más información acerca de esa exención, por favor, vea:Ejercicio de Autoridad de 2022 (Cierto Apoyo Significado Limitado y Apoyo Significativo  Relevante para las Organizaciones Designadas)5 de febrero de 2014, Ejercicio de Autoridad (Cierto Apoyo Significado Limitado para las Organizaciones  Designadas)10 de agosto de 2022, Memorándum de Políticas de USCIS, Implementación y Autoridad de Exención Discrecional Bajo la Ley de Inmigración y Nacionalidad (INA) § 212(d)(3)(B)(i) para la Provisión de Cierto Apoyo Significativo Limitado y Apoyo Significativo  Relevante para las Organizaciones Designadas8 de mayo de 2015, Memorándum de Políticas de USCIS, Implementación de la Exención Discrecional de Autoridad bajo la Sección 212(d)(3)(B)(i) de INA para la Disposición de cierto Apoyo Significativo LimitadoEnlaces RelacionadosCausales de Inadmisibilidad Relacionadas con el Terrorismo (TRIG)Exenciones a las Causales de Inadmisibilidad Relacionadas con el TerrorismoCausales de Inadmisibilidad Relacionadas con el Terrorismo (TRIG ) - Exenciones a Grupos Última Revisión/Actualización: 01/24/2025 Causales de Inadmisibilidad Relacionadas/ al Terrorismo (TRIG) - Exenciones Situacionales Los secretarios del Departamento de Estado y del Departamento de Seguridad Nacional, en consulta con el fiscal general, podrían autorizar exenciones de casuales de inadmisibilidad relacionadas con el Terrorismo (TRIG). Vea la sección 212(d)(3)(B) de la Ley de Inmigración y Nacionalidad (INA). Estas exenciones solo aplican a personas que participan o que probablemente participen después de entrar en actividades terroristas (Ver sección 212(a)(E)(B)(i)(II) de INA.A continuación encontrará más información acerca de cada una de las exenciones aprobadas hasta el momento.Funcionarios Públicos AfgasEmpleo como Funcionario Público en AfganistánEl 8 de junio de 2022, los secretarios de Seguridad Nacional y de Estado, en consulta entre sí y con el fiscal general, autorizaron una exención de ciertas causales de inadmisibilidad relacionadas con el terrorismo para ciertos solicitantes que fueron empleados como funcionarios públicos en Afganistán bajo los talibanes, específicamente, en cualquier momento desde el 27 de septiembre de 1996 hasta el 21 de diciembre de 2001, o a partir del 15 de agosto de 2021. Esta exención reemplaza un ejercicio similar de autoridad emitido el 18 de enero de 2017 y amplía el período cubierto para incluir el período a partir del 15 de agosto de 2021.Muchas personas que trabajaban en puestos de la administración pública en Afganistán antes del 27 de septiembre de 1996 continuaron haciéndolo después de esa fecha. Muchos lo hicieron bajo coacción u otras situaciones de dificultad. En otros casos, las personas utilizaron sus posiciones en capacidades humanitarias para mitigar las acciones represivas del régimen talibán, a do con gran riesgo personal. Posteriormente, algus de estos funcionarios públicos trabajaron para la Fuerza Internacional de Asistencia para la Seguridad, el gobier de Estados Unidos o el gobier afga que se estableció el 22 de diciembre de 2001, o prestaron asistencia a ellos. Algunas personas continuaron proporcionando servicios gubernamentales esenciales incluso después del colapso del gobier de Kabul el 15 de agosto de 2021. Esta exención permite discreción para abordar estos en adjudicaciones individuales y para cumplir con las obligaciones humanitarias de los Estados Unidos al tiempo que garantiza la seguridad e integridad de su sistema de inmigración.Para obtener más información sobre esta exención, consulte:Ejercicio de Autoridad de 2022 (Funcionario Público Afga)10 de agosto de 2022, Memorándum de Políticas de USCIS, Implementación y Autoridad de Exención Discrecional Bajo la Ley de Inmigración y Nacionalidad (INA) § 212(d)(3)(B)(i) para los Funcionarios Públicos AfgasAliados AfgasPersonas que participan en actividades de resistencia en la promoción de los intereses de los Estados UnidosEl 8 de junio de 2022, los secretarios de Seguridad Nacional y de Estado, en consulta entre sí y con el fiscal general, autorizaron una exención a ciertas causales de inadmisibilidad relacionadas con el terrorismo para los aliados afgas que apoyaron los intereses de Estados Unidos o participaron en el movimiento de resistencia contra los talibanes y otras organizaciones afiliadas, o contra la ocupación soviética de Afganistán.La participación del gobier de Estados Unidos en los asuntos afgas siempre ha dependido estrechamente de la participación de ciudadas afgas alineados con los objetivos del gobier de Estados Unidos en la región. Desde el momento de la resistencia a la agresión soviética, a través de la lucha contra el gobier del opresivo régimen talibán que permitió los ataques del 9/11 contra Estados Unidos, y durante los esfuerzos de los últimos 20 años para instalar un gobier estable y democrático frente a una creciente insurgencia, la política y los intereses estadounidenses han dependido de los valientes sacrificios de los ciudadas afgas comunes.Esta exención permite discreción para abordar estos problemas en adjudicaciones individuales y para cumplir con las obligaciones humanitarias de los Estados Unidos al tiempo que garantiza la seguridad e integridad de su sistema de inmigración.Para obtener más información sobre esta exención, consulte:Ejercicio de Autoridad (Los Aliados Afgas)10 de agosto de 2022, Memorándum de Políticas de USCIS, Implementación y Autoridad de Exención Discrecional Bajo la Ley de Inmigración y Nacionalidad (INA) § 212(d)(3)(B)(i) para los Aliados AfgasApoyo Significativo Bajo CoerciónSe pueden otorgar exenciones para solicitantes que provean apoyo significativo bajo coerción a organizaciones terroristas determinadas o  determinadas, que, como mínimo, requiere que el apoyo significativo haya sido requerido en respuesta a una amenaza razonablemente percibida de daño grave. Un ejemplo de apoyo significativo bajo coerción podría incluir proporcionar dinero o un servicio (como, por ejemplo, transportar combatientes y suministros) a un grupo rebelde bajo amenaza a punta de pistola para obedecer con tal demanda.Para más información acerca de la Exención por Proporcionar Apoyo Significativo a una Organización Terrorista  Designada, por favor vea:El 26 de febrero de 2007, cometer una actividad terrorista, o a un miembro de una organización terrorista según describe la sección 212(a)(3)(B)(vi) de la INA. Un ejemplo de la disposición de cuidado médico podría incluir el proporcionar servicios en la capacidad de un profesional médico a miembros de una organización terrorista.Para más información acerca de esta exención, por favor vea:El 13 de octubre de 2011, Ejercicio de Autoridad (Disposición Voluntaria de Cuidado Médico)El 20 de viembre de 2011, Memorándum de Implementación de USCIS, Implementación de una Nueva Exención Discrecional Bajo la Sección 212(d)(3)(B)(i) de la INA por Provisión de Apoyo Significativo en Forma de Cuidado MédicoCiertos Solicitantes que Tienen Beneficios de Inmigración Actualmente (Exención General Limitada)El 10 de agosto de 2012, luego de una consulta con el secretario del Estado y el fiscal general, el secretario de seguridad nacional usó su autoridad discrecional para  aplicar los párrafos (iv)(IV), (iv)(V), (iv)(VI), y (i)(VIII) de la sección 212(a)(3)(B) de la INA, 8 U.S.C. § 1182(a)(3)(B), a ciertos extranjeros cualificados que tienen beneficios de inmigración actuales, excepto una visa de  inmigrante, que actualmente sean inadmisibles bajo las subsecciones aplicables de la sección 212(a)(3)(B)(i) de INA, debido a asociaciones anteriores (nivel III) con organizaciones terroristas  designadas. Específicamente, el uso de autoridad permite la exención de las siguientes actividades:Solicitar fondos u otros artículos de valor;Solicitarle a cualquier persona su membresía en dicha organización;Proporcionar apoyo significativo a la organización; oRecibir entrenamiento militar de, o de parte de, una organización terrorista cualificada bajo el nivel III.Para más información acerca de esa exención, por favor vea:17 de agosto de 2012, Ejercicio de Autoridad (Exención General Limitado)26 de septiembre de 2012, Implementación de una Nueva Exención Discrecional General Limitada bajo la Sección 212(d)(3)(B)(i) de INA para Solicitantes Cualificados con Asociaciones y Actividades Específicas con Organizaciones Terroristas Cualificadas  Designadas, o “Clasificación III.Levantamientos IraquíesEl 17 de agosto de 2012, el secretario de seguridad nacional, en consulta con el secretario del Estado y el fiscal general, usaron su autoridad discrecional para  aplicar la mayoría de las casuales de inadmisibilidad relacionadas con terrorismo a ciertos solicitantes que participaron en los levantamientos iraquíes en contra del gobier de Saddam Hussein en Irak entre el 1 de marzo y el 5 de abril de 1991.Para más información acerca de esa exención, por favor vea:7 de agosto de 2012, Ejercicio de Autoridad (Levantamientos Iraquíes)12 de viembre de 2012, Memorándum de Implementación de USCIS, Implementación de una Nueva Exención Bajo la Sección 212(d)(3)(B)(i) de la INA por Participación en Los Levantamientos IraquíesCierto Apoyo Significativo LimitadoEl 5 de febrero de 2014, los secretarios de Seguridad Nacional y de Estado, luego de una reunión con el fiscal general usaron su autoridad discrecional para  aplicar la casual de inadmisibilidad a ciertos solicitantes que proporcionaron cierto apoyo significativo limitado a organizaciones terroristas  designadas, o a un miembro de dicho tipo de organización. Vea la sección 212(d)(3)(B) de la Ley de Inmigración y Nacionalidad (INA). Estas exenciones solo aplican a personas que participan o que probablemente participen después de entrar en actividades terroristas (Ver sección 212(a)(E)(B)(i)(II) de INA.A continuación encontrará más información acerca de cada una de las exenciones aprobadas hasta el momento.Funcionarios Públicos AfgasEmpleo como Funcionario Público en AfganistánEl 8 de junio de 2022, los secretarios de Seguridad Nacional y de Estado, en consulta entre sí y con el fiscal general, autorizaron una exención de ciertas causales de inadmisibilidad relacionadas con el terrorismo para ciertos solicitantes que fueron empleados como funcionarios públicos en Afganistán bajo los talibanes, específicamente, en cualquier momento desde el 27 de septiembre de 1996 hasta el 21 de diciembre de 2001, o a partir del 15 de agosto de 2021. Esta exención reemplaza un ejercicio similar de autoridad emitido el 18 de enero de 2017 y amplía el período cubierto para incluir el período a partir del 15 de agosto de 2021.Muchas personas que trabajaban en puestos de la administración pública en Afganistán antes del 27 de septiembre de 1996 continuaron haciéndolo después de esa fecha. Muchos lo hicieron bajo coacción u otras situaciones de dificultad. En otros casos, las personas utilizaron sus posiciones en capacidades humanitarias para mitigar las acciones represivas del régimen talibán, a do con gran riesgo personal. Posteriormente, algus de estos funcionarios públicos trabajaron para la Fuerza Internacional de Asistencia para la Seguridad, el gobier de Estados Unidos o el gobier afga que se estableció el 22 de diciembre de 2001, o prestaron asistencia a ellos. Algunas personas continuaron proporcionando servicios gubernamentales esenciales incluso después del colapso del gobier de Kabul el 15 de agosto de 2021. Esta exención permite discreción para abordar estos en adjudicaciones individuales y para cumplir con las obligaciones humanitarias de los Estados Unidos al tiempo que garantiza la seguridad e integridad de su sistema de inmigración.Para obtener más información sobre esta exención, consulte:Ejercicio de Autoridad de 2022 (Funcionario Público Afga)10 de agosto de 2022, Memorándum de Políticas de USCIS, Implementación y Autoridad de Exención Discrecional Bajo la Ley de Inmigración y Nacionalidad (INA) § 212(d)(3)(B)(i) para los Funcionarios Públicos AfgasAliados AfgasPersonas que participan en actividades de resistencia en la promoción de los intereses de los Estados UnidosEl 8 de junio de 2022, los secretarios de Seguridad Nacional y de Estado, en consulta entre sí y con el fiscal general, autorizaron una exención a ciertas causales de inadmisibilidad relacionadas con el terrorismo para los aliados afgas que apoyaron los intereses de Estados Unidos o participaron en el movimiento de resistencia contra los talibanes y otras organizaciones afiliadas, o contra la ocupación soviética de Afganistán.La participación del gobier de Estados Unidos en los asuntos afgas siempre ha dependido estrechamente de la participación de ciudadas afgas alineados con los objetivos del gobier de Estados Unidos en la región. Desde el momento de la resistencia a la agresión soviética, a través de la lucha contra el gobier del opresivo régimen talibán que permitió los ataques del 9/11 contra Estados Unidos, y durante los esfuerzos de los últimos 20 años para instalar un gobier estable y democrático frente a una creciente insurgencia, la política y los intereses estadounidenses han dependido de los valientes sacrificios de los ciudadas afgas comunes.Esta exención permite discreción para abordar estos problemas en adjudicaciones individuales y para cumplir con las obligaciones humanitarias de los Estados Unidos al tiempo que garantiza la seguridad e integridad de su sistema de inmigración.Para obtener más información sobre esta exención, consulte:Ejercicio de Autoridad (Los Aliados Afgas)10 de agosto de 2022, Memorándum de Políticas de USCIS, Implementación y Autoridad de Exención Discrecional Bajo la Ley de Inmigración y Nacionalidad (INA) § 212(d)(3)(B)(i) para los Aliados AfgasApoyo Significativo Bajo CoerciónSe pueden otorgar exenciones para solicitantes que provean apoyo significativo bajo coerción a organizaciones terroristas determinadas o  determinadas, que, como mínimo, requiere que el apoyo significativo haya sido requerido en respuesta a una amenaza razonablemente percibida de daño grave. Un ejemplo de apoyo significativo bajo coerción podría incluir proporcionar dinero o un servicio (como, por ejemplo, transportar combatientes y suministros) a un grupo rebelde bajo amenaza a punta de pistola para obedecer con tal demanda.Para más información acerca de la Exención por Proporcionar Apoyo Significativo a una Organización Terrorista  Designada, por favor vea:El 26 de febrero de 2007, Pending Applications for Employment-Based Preference Categories as of April 3, 2025 (XLSX, 103.87 KB) June 30, 2025 Inventory report intended to provide information about the number of pending Forms I-485 in the employment-based preference categories. The report provides our estimate of how many Forms I-485 we have in our inventory for each employment-based preference category, by selected country of chargeability, and by the month and year of the estimated priority date. An alien with a pending adjustment of status application can use the report to estimate how many Forms I-485 we have in our inventory with earlier priority dates for their employment-based preference category and country of chargeability. Wait times for an employment-based immigrant visa depend on numerous factors, including, but t limited to, supply of visas and demand of visas for a particular preference category (at USCIS and the Department of State (DOS)), priority date, the country to which a visa will be charged (usually an applicant’s country of birth), and statutory limitations (for example, per country caps). Please te, that this report does t contain information about DOS inventory, r does it have any information about aliens with pending or approved immigrant visa petitions who have t yet applied for adjustment of status. Additional FAQs about this report. ## Page 305: Eligible to Naturalize Dashboard | USCIS
URL: https://www.uscis.gov/tools/reports-and-studies/immigration-and-citizenship-data/eligible-to-naturalize-dashboard
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Eligible to Naturalize Dashboard The Eligible to Naturalize Dashboard displays data on the population of lawful permanent residents (LPRs) who may be eligible to naturalize. The data capture country of birth, state, and core-based statistical area (CBSA) and include people who obtained LPR status since fiscal year 2010 and have t filed a Form N-400, Application for Naturalization, to become a U.S. citizen.The Fact Sheets on Promoting Citizenship were developed to help promote naturalization to individuals with specific circumstances, such as low-income individuals, individuals experiencing homelessness, individuals who frequently travel, individuals age 50 and older, individuals who previously had certain immigration status (asylees, refugees, special immigrant juveniles, or T and U visa holders) and individuals who obtain lawful permanent residence following a grant of Cancellation of Removal or Suspension of Deportation. The data capture country of birth, state, and core-based statistical area (CBSA) and include people who obtained LPR status since fiscal year 2010 and have t filed a Form N-400, Application for Naturalization, to become a U.S. citizen.The Fact Sheets on Promoting Citizenship were developed to help promote naturalization to individuals with specific circumstances, such as low-income individuals, individuals experiencing homelessness, individuals who frequently travel, individuals age 50 and older, individuals who previously had certain immigration status (asylees, refugees, special immigrant juveniles, or T and U visa holders) and individuals who obtain lawful permanent residence following a grant of Cancellation of Removal or Suspension of Deportation. ## Page 306: Civil Surgeons: How to Report Gonorrhea Screening Results on Form I-693 | USCIS
URL: https://www.uscis.gov/tools/designated-civil-surgeons/civil-surgeons-how-to-report-gonorrhea-screening-results-on-form-i-693
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Civil Surgeons: How to Report Gorrhea Screening Results on Form I-693 Effective Aug. 1, 2016, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) issued new Technical Instructions that require gorrhea testing for most adjustment of status applicants 15 years of age and older who are required to have a full medical examination when they file Form I-485, Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status.If the applicant’s Form I-693, Report of Medical Examination and Vaccination Record, was completed before Aug. 1, 2016, they do t need to report results of such testing, and officers should t issue a Request for Evidence. A Form I-693 is considered completed on the date the civil surgeon signs the form’s certification statement. (See USCIS Policy Manual Volume 8--Admissibility, Part B. Health-Related Grounds of Inadmissibility, Chapter 4--Review of Medical Documentation, C.--Documentation Completed by Civil Surgeon, 3.--Signatures.)Who Must Be Tested for GorrheaWhile most adjustment of status applicants 15 years of age and older must be tested for gorrhea, certain applicants are exempt from having to submit a full medical examination and do t need to be tested. (See USCIS Policy Manual Volume 8--Admissibility, Part B. Health-Related Grounds of Inadmissibility, Chapter 3—Applicability of Medical Examination Vaccination Requirements, A. Requirements by Benefit Type.)The following applicants may submit Form I-693 with only a completed Vaccination Record (and the information/signature sections for the applicant and civil surgeons), provided they had a medical examination abroad in which the panel physician did t identify a Class A condition:Refugees.Derivative asylees who file an adjustment application within one year of becoming eligible to file.K and V nimmigrants who file an adjustment application within one year of the medical examination abroad.The chart below summarizes who must be tested and who does t.If the applicant…And the applicant is…Does the applicant need to be tested for gorrhea?Is required to receive a full medical examination15 years of age or olderYounger than 15 years of ageOnly if there is a history of gorrhea or reason to suspect an infection with gorrhea.Is T required to receive a full medical examinationAny ageHow Do Civil Surgeons Complete Form I-693 to Report Gorrhea Testing Results?Civil surgeons report the results of gorrhea testing in Part 7, Section C of Form I-693 (version date of Feb. 7, 2017, with expiration date of Feb. 28, 2019). CDC Rescinds Requirement for Documentation of Gorrhea TestingWhen the CDC issued the Technical Instructions requiring adding of gorrhea testing results in Forms I-693 completed on or after Aug. 1, 2016, it also required civil surgeons to attach all medical documentation such as laboratory reports to the Form I-693, regardless of whether the test results were negative or positive. However, on March 15, 2017, the CDC updated the Technical Instructions to say laboratory reports and  medical documentation do t need to be included with Form I-693. This removal of the documentation requirement applies both prospectively and retroactively, as well as to both the new and previous versions of Form I-693.As a result of the updated Gorrhea TIs, USCIS may adjudicate an adjustment application using an wise properly filed and completed Form I-693, regardless of whether or t the civil surgeon attached documentation of gorrhea testing results.If You Need More InformationCivil surgeons who have medical questions about the new gorrhea screening requirements should contact CDC directly at www.cdc.gov/info.If you are t registered with USCIS to receive civil surgeon updates, we suggest that you register through the USCIS Get  Updates web page. Please ensure that s from USCIS are t caught in your spam filter or diverted to your junk  folder. ## Page 307: Vaccination Requirements | USCIS
URL: https://www.uscis.gov/tools/designated-civil-surgeons/vaccination-requirements
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Vaccination Requirements These Questions and Answers provide basic information about the general vaccination requirements for immigrants (including aliens seeking adjustment of status), and specifically about the assessment made by the civil surgeon to determine whether an alien meets the vaccination requirements. These Questions and Answers do t address the vaccination assessments conducted by panel physicians overseas.For refugees applying for adjustment of status, health department physicians may complete only the vaccination record portion of Form I-693, Report of Medical Examination and Vaccination Record, as blanket-designated civil surgeons.BackgroundUnder the immigration laws of the United States, an alien who applies for an immigrant visa abroad, or who seeks to adjust status to that of a lawful permanent resident while in the United States, is required to receive vaccinations to prevent the following diseases:Mumps;Measles;Rubella;Polio;Tetanus and Diphtheria Toxoids;Pertussis;Haemophilus influenzae type B;Hepatitis B; andAny  vaccine-preventable diseases recommended by the Advisory Committee for Immunization Practices (ACIP). The ACIP is an advisory committee to the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)/Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) that recommends immunizations for the general U.S. population. Since Dec.14, 2009, when the ACIP recommends new vaccines for the general U.S. population, CDC assesses whether these vaccines should be required for immigration purposes on a regular and on an as-needed basis according to specific criteria set by CDC.CDC is responsible for publishing the Technical Instructions for Civil Surgeons. These documents and the HHS regulations set the requirements for the immigration medical examination and are binding on civil surgeons (See the CDC Vaccination Technical Instructions for Civil Surgeons and 42 C.F.R. Section 34.3). The Technical Instructions include a vaccination component, specifying how the civil surgeon has to conduct the vaccination assessment. The civil surgeon records the results of the immigration medical examination, including the results of the vaccination assessment, on USCIS Form I-693.If an alien applies for an immigrant visa abroad, that individual has to undergo an immigration medical examination conducted by a panel physician authorized by the U.S. Department of State (DOS). CDC issues separate instructions to panel physicians designated by DOS to conduct immigration medical examinations abroad. For more information about panel physicians, please consult CDC’s and DOS's websitesTechnical Instructions for Panel Physicians | CDCMedical Examinations FAQs (state.gov).Questions and AnswersQ. Where can I find information about vaccinations in general?A. CDC publishes information about vaccinations in general and information about the vaccine requirements for immigration purposes at www.cdc.gov/vaccines/.Q. Why do immigrants (including adjustment of status applicants) have to show proof they have received certain vaccinations?A. Under the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) section 212(a)(1)(A)(ii), an alien who seeks admission as an immigrant or who seeks adjustment of status to that of a lawful permanent resident, who fails to show proof that they were vaccinated against vaccine-preventable diseases, is inadmissible and therefore ineligible for admission or adjustment of status.Q. How does the CDC decide which vaccines are required for immigration purposes?A. Some of the vaccines that are required are specifically listed in INA section 212(a)(1)(A)(ii). In addition to these, the statute also requires that an individual receive any  vaccinations recommended by the ACIP. CDC uses the following criteria in determining which of these recommended vaccines should be required for immigration purposes:The vaccine must be an age-appropriate vaccine as recommended by the ACIP for the general U.S. population; andAt least one of the following:The vaccine must protect against a disease that has the potential to cause an outbreak; orThe vaccine must protect against a disease eliminated in the United States,or is in the process of being eliminated in the United States.Q. I am seeking adjustment of status but already completed an immigration medical examination abroad completed by a panel physician and also received some vaccines. Do I have to repeat the immigration medical examination and get the vaccines again?A. Some applicants who have previously completed an immigration medical examination abroad, including applicants applying for adjustment of status as refugees, are t required to repeat the entire immigration medical examination when they apply for adjustment. Please read the instructions to Form I-693 to determine if you must repeat the immigration medical examination, including the vaccination assessment, based on your current status in the United States and the immigration category under which you are applying for adjustment of status. For more information see USCIS Policy Manual Applicability of Medical Examination and Vaccination Requirement.Q. How do I kw which vaccines are required for immigration purposes?A. A civil surgeon is required to follow the Technical Instructions for Civil Surgeons. CDC publishes the vaccination requirements and immigration medical examination instructions (including a detailed table listing all required vaccines).Q. Do I have to receive all the required vaccines, even though I have been vaccinated before?A. . The civil surgeon will review your vaccination records at the time of your immigration medical examination to see whether you have proof of required vaccinations against vaccine-preventable diseases that are appropriate for your age category. It is important that you take any written vaccination documentation you may have to the civil surgeon when you have your immigration medical examination.If you lack any vaccinations required for your age category, the civil surgeon will administer the vaccines as needed. In the alternative, you can also choose to obtain the required vaccines from your private healthcare provider. However, because only a civil surgeon is authorized to complete the vaccination assessment on the Form I-693, you must return to the civil surgeon with the proof that you have received the missing vaccines.In addition, some individuals are immune to vaccine-preventable diseases, and they kw of the immunity because their private healthcare provider has tested them. If you have any written evidence of immunity, you should take this documentation to your civil surgeon. This will enable the civil surgeon to determine which vaccines you need to receive.Q. Do I have to receive all the vaccines on CDC's vaccination list for the immigrant population, or only the ones that are age appropriate?A. You are required to document receipt of vaccines that are age appropriate for you. The civil surgeon will antate Form I-693 to indicate that you were t required to receive a particular vaccine because it was t age appropriate at the time of the immigration medical examination.Q. Do I have to receive all the vaccines that are on CDC's list and that are age appropriate, if I have a medical condition that prevents me from receiving the required vaccines?A. If you have a medical condition that prevents you from receiving a vaccine that is appropriate for your age, the civil surgeon will antate the Form I-693 accordingly and mark the vaccine as contraindicated. A contraindication is a condition that prevents you from receiving a particular vaccine. CDC lists in its Technical Instructions what is considered a contraindication. It is up to the civil surgeon to determine whether you have such a condition that prevents you from receiving a particular vaccine at the time of the immigration medical examination.Q. Certain vaccine series can only be completed with multiple visits to the civil surgeon. Am I required to complete the entire series before the civil surgeon can sign the Form I-693?A. You are only required to receive a single dose of each vaccine when you visit the civil surgeon. You are encouraged to follow up with your private health care provider to complete the series. Once you have received the single dose appropriate at the time, the civil surgeon can sign and certify the Form I-693.Q. I am pregnant and do t wish to receive any vaccinations. Do I still have to get them to be able to obtain permanent resident status in the United States?A. If you are pregnant, the CDC's Technical Instructions direct the civil surgeon how to evaluate the vaccines you are able to receive during pregnancy. If the civil surgeon cant safely administer a required vaccine, they will antate the Form I-693 by marking the vaccine as contraindicated. See the CDC “Guidelines for Vaccinating Pregnant Women” page for information on pregnancy and vaccinations in general. If the Technical Instructions mandate that a specific vaccine is t contraindicated by pregnancy, but you want to wait to receive the vaccine until after your pregnancy, you may choose to delay the completion of your immigration medical examination until that time. Once you receive the required vaccine(s) and all  requirements, the civil surgeon can then sign and complete your immigration medical examination. However, you should be aware that this could delay the processing of your application for adjustment of status.Q. Can the civil surgeon safely administer all vaccines that are required all at once?A. The civil surgeon will let you kw if you can receive all the vaccines at once, or if there is a concern based on your particular medical condition that will t allow you to receive all required vaccines at once.Q. When does the flu season start for purposes of the seasonal flu vaccine requirement? Since the seasonal flu vaccine is required, do I have to get the seasonal flu vaccine if it is t the flu season?A. For purposes of the immigration medical examination, the civil surgeon is required to administer the flu vaccine from Sept.1 until March 31. If your immigration medical examination is during a period when the flu vaccine is available to your civil surgeon, you must receive it. If you have an immigration medical examination completed when the flu vaccine is t available to your civil surgeon, then you are t required to document that you have received the seasonal flu vaccine for immigration purposes.Q. Who pays for the vaccinations?A. You are responsible for paying the appropriate fee for all vaccinations. If the civil surgeon is administering the vaccinations, you are responsible for paying the appropriate fee directly to the civil surgeon, as agreed upon with the civil surgeon. You should ask about the price of the vaccinations before the immigration medical examination or the administration of the vaccinations. USCIS does t regulate the fees charged by civil surgeons for the completion of an immigration medical examination. Rates may vary by civil surgeon. It may be helpful to call several local civil surgeons to compare fees. For more information on how to obtain a good faith estimate prior to your appointment, please visit: Understanding costs in advance.Q. Can I be forced to be vaccinated for immigration purposes?A. If you refuse to receive the vaccines required for immigration purposes, as mandated by the immigration laws of the United States, your application for legal permanent resident status may be denied.Q. What will happen if I refuse to receive one or all of the required vaccines?A. Tell the civil surgeon if you do t wish to receive the required vaccines or a particular vaccine. You should also tell the civil surgeon the reason you do t wish to receive the vaccine(s). In this case, a waiver may be available to you, but only under the following circumstances:You are opposed to all vaccinations in any form– a waiver may t be granted if you only object to specific vaccinations;Your objection must be based on religious beliefs or moral convictions; andThe religious or moral beliefs must be sincere.The form used to apply for a waiver depends on the adjustment category under which you are seeking legal permanent residence status. For example, refugees and asylees seeking adjustment of status should file Form I-602, Application by Refugee for Waiver of Grounds of Excludability. Individuals seeking adjustment of status based on an approved Form I-130, Petition for Alien Relative, or Form I-140, Immigrant Petition for Alien Worker, are required to file Form I-601, Application for Waiver of Grounds of Inadmissibility.Q. My civil surgeon says that a vaccine is currently t available. What should I do?A. Ask the civil surgeon whether ather health care provider may have the vaccine. If ather physician or department or pharmacy carries the vaccine and can administer the vaccine, you should get the vaccine and request documentation that you have received the vaccine. Bring the written record back to the civil surgeon so that they can complete the Form I-693.HHS/CDC monitors which vaccines are t available in the United States, or which vaccines may experience a shortage. If CDC determines there is a nation-wide shortage of a vaccine, it will recommend to USCIS to post a message on uscis.gov to explain to applicants and civil surgeons whether the vaccine is required and under what circumstances. The information is available on USCIS’ Form I-693 page, the Immigration Medical Examination page, or the Designated Civil Surgeon page.Q. Will USCIS accept a Form I-693 if the vaccination chart is incomplete?A. . The vaccination chart should have at least one entry in each row for each vaccine. If the vaccination chart is t properly completed at the time of the immigration medical examination, USCIS may return the Form I-693 to you with instructions on how to correct it.If you refuse a vaccine because of religious or moral reasons, the civil surgeon will mark this on the Form I-693. In this case, you are inadmissible and will have to apply for a waiver of inadmissibility.Q: Where can I find more information about the vaccination requirements for immigration purposes and how these requirements affect the completion of Form I-693?A. CDC publishes the Technical Instructions for Civil Surgeons, including the vaccination requirements. For more information about the civil surgeon program, the completion of Form I-693, or the adjustment of status application, please visit uscis.gov, or call the USCIS Contact Center at 800-375-5283 (TTY 800-767-1833).Q: Did the CDC’s Vaccination Technical Instructions change for the polio vaccine?A: On May 1, 2024, the Vaccination Technical Instructions for Civil Surgeons changed for the polio vaccine. One dose of IPV should be given to anyone 2 months or older if they are t currently up to date according to ACIP recommendations, including adults who cant show proof of the childhood vaccine series. If the Form I-693 was signed by a civil surgeon on or after May 1, 2024, the new polio vaccine requirement applies.Q: Is the COVID-19 vaccine required for aliens applying for adjustment of status?A. . As of Jan. 20, 2025, aliens applying for adjustment of status are  longer required to provide documentation of having received the COVID-19 vaccination. Therefore, for any adjustment of status application pending on or after January 20, 2025, the alien applying does t need to provide documentation of having completed the COVID-19 vaccination. Prior to Jan. 20, 2025, the COVID-19 vaccine was required based on age. See the chart below for details:COVID-19 Vaccination Requirements Before Jan. 20, 2025Date Civil Surgeon Signed Form I-693Age Required to Receive COVID-19 Vaccination or after Oct. 1, 202112 years of age and olderOn or after v. 3, 20215 years of age and olderOn or after July 25, 20226 months of age and olderRelated LinksVaccination Technical Instructions for Civil Surgeons | CDC Form I-693, Report of Medical Examination and Vaccination RecordCDC: Vaccines and Immunizations42 CFR Part 34.4 Medical tificationsCDC: Guidelines for Vaccinating Pregnant Women Last Reviewed/Updated: 07/08/2025 Vaccination Requirements These Questions and Answers provide basic information about the general vaccination requirements for immigrants (including aliens seeking adjustment of status), and specifically about the assessment made by the civil surgeon to determine whether an alien meets the vaccination requirements. Why do immigrants (including adjustment of status applicants) have to show proof they have received certain vaccinations?A. Under the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) section 212(a)(1)(A)(ii), an alien who seeks admission as an immigrant or who seeks adjustment of status to that of a lawful permanent resident, who fails to show proof that they were vaccinated against vaccine-preventable diseases, is inadmissible and therefore ineligible for admission or adjustment of status.Q. How does the CDC decide which vaccines are required for immigration purposes?A. Some of the vaccines that are required are specifically listed in INA section 212(a)(1)(A)(ii). In addition to these, the statute also requires that an individual receive any  vaccinations recommended by the ACIP. CDC uses the following criteria in determining which of these recommended vaccines should be required for immigration purposes:The vaccine must be an age-appropriate vaccine as recommended by the ACIP for the general U.S. population; andAt least one of the following:The vaccine must protect against a disease that has the potential to cause an outbreak; orThe vaccine must protect against a disease eliminated in the United States,or is in the process of being eliminated in the United States.Q. I am seeking adjustment of status but already completed an immigration medical examination abroad completed by a panel physician and also received some vaccines. Do I have to repeat the immigration medical examination and get the vaccines again?A. Some applicants who have previously completed an immigration medical examination abroad, including applicants applying for adjustment of status as refugees, are t required to repeat the entire immigration medical examination when they apply for adjustment. Please read the instructions to Form I-693 to determine if you must repeat the immigration medical examination, including the vaccination assessment, based on your current status in the United States and the immigration category under which you are applying for adjustment of status. For more information see USCIS Policy Manual Applicability of Medical Examination and Vaccination Requirement.Q. How do I kw which vaccines are required for immigration purposes?A. A civil surgeon is required to follow the Technical Instructions for Civil Surgeons. CDC publishes the vaccination requirements and immigration medical examination instructions (including a detailed table listing all required vaccines).Q. Do I have to receive all the required vaccines, even though I have been vaccinated before?A. . The civil surgeon will review your vaccination records at the time of your immigration medical examination to see whether you have proof of required vaccinations against vaccine-preventable diseases that are appropriate for your age category. It is important that you take any written vaccination documentation you may have to the civil surgeon when you have your immigration medical examination.If you lack any vaccinations required for your age category, the civil surgeon will administer the vaccines as needed. In the alternative, you can also choose to obtain the required vaccines from your private healthcare provider. However, because only a civil surgeon is authorized to complete the vaccination assessment on the Form I-693, you must return to the civil surgeon with the proof that you have received the missing vaccines.In addition, some individuals are immune to vaccine-preventable diseases, and they kw of the immunity because their private healthcare provider has tested them. If you have any written evidence of immunity, you should take this documentation to your civil surgeon. This will enable the civil surgeon to determine which vaccines you need to receive.Q. Do I have to receive all the vaccines on CDC's vaccination list for the immigrant population, or only the ones that are age appropriate?A. You are required to document receipt of vaccines that are age appropriate for you. The civil surgeon will antate Form I-693 to indicate that you were t required to receive a particular vaccine because it was t age appropriate at the time of the immigration medical examination.Q. Do I have to receive all the vaccines that are on CDC's list and that are age appropriate, if I have a medical condition that prevents me from receiving the required vaccines?A. If you have a medical condition that prevents you from receiving a vaccine that is appropriate for your age, the civil surgeon will antate the Form I-693 accordingly and mark the vaccine as contraindicated. A contraindication is a condition that prevents you from receiving a particular vaccine. CDC lists in its Technical Instructions what is considered a contraindication. It is up to the civil surgeon to determine whether you have such a condition that prevents you from receiving a particular vaccine at the time of the immigration medical examination.Q. Certain vaccine series can only be completed with multiple visits to the civil surgeon. Am I required to complete the entire series before the civil surgeon can sign the Form I-693?A. You are only required to receive a single dose of each vaccine when you visit the civil surgeon. You are encouraged to follow up with your private health care provider to complete the series. Once you have received the single dose appropriate at the time, the civil surgeon can sign and certify the Form I-693.Q. I am pregnant and do t wish to receive any vaccinations. Do I still have to get them to be able to obtain permanent resident status in the United States?A. If you are pregnant, the CDC's Technical Instructions direct the civil surgeon how to evaluate the vaccines you are able to receive during pregnancy. If the civil surgeon cant safely administer a required vaccine, they will antate the Form I-693 by marking the vaccine as contraindicated. See the CDC “Guidelines for Vaccinating Pregnant Women” page for information on pregnancy and vaccinations in general. If the Technical Instructions mandate that a specific vaccine is t contraindicated by pregnancy, but you want to wait to receive the vaccine until after your pregnancy, you may choose to delay the completion of your immigration medical examination until that time. Once you receive the required vaccine(s) and all  requirements, the civil surgeon can then sign and complete your immigration medical examination. However, you should be aware that this could delay the processing of your application for adjustment of status.Q. Can the civil surgeon safely administer all vaccines that are required all at once?A. The civil surgeon will let you kw if you can receive all the vaccines at once, or if there is a concern based on your particular medical condition that will t allow you to receive all required vaccines at once.Q. When does the flu season start for purposes of the seasonal flu vaccine requirement? Since the seasonal flu vaccine is required, do I have to get the seasonal flu vaccine if it is t the flu season?A. For purposes of the immigration medical examination, the civil surgeon is required to administer the flu vaccine from Sept.1 until March 31. If your immigration medical examination is during a period when the flu vaccine is available to your civil surgeon, you must receive it. If you have an immigration medical examination completed when the flu vaccine is t available to your civil surgeon, then you are t required to document that you have received the seasonal flu vaccine for immigration purposes.Q. Who pays for the vaccinations?A. You are responsible for paying the appropriate fee for all vaccinations. If the civil surgeon is administering the vaccinations, you are responsible for paying the appropriate fee directly to the civil surgeon, as agreed upon with the civil surgeon. You should ask about the price of the vaccinations before the immigration medical examination or the administration of the vaccinations. USCIS does t regulate the fees charged by civil surgeons for the completion of an immigration medical examination. Rates may vary by civil surgeon. It may be helpful to call several local civil surgeons to compare fees. For more information on how to obtain a good faith estimate prior to your appointment, please visit: Understanding costs in advance.Q. Can I be forced to be vaccinated for immigration purposes?A. If you refuse to receive the vaccines required for immigration purposes, as mandated by the immigration laws of the United States, your application for legal permanent resident status may be denied.Q. What will happen if I refuse to receive one or all of the required vaccines?A. Tell the civil surgeon if you do t wish to receive the required vaccines or a particular vaccine. You should also tell the civil surgeon the reason you do t wish to receive the vaccine(s). In this case, a waiver may be available to you, but only under the following circumstances:You are opposed to all vaccinations in any form– a waiver may t be granted if you only object to specific vaccinations;Your objection must be based on religious beliefs or moral convictions; andThe religious or moral beliefs must be sincere.The form used to apply for a waiver depends on the adjustment category under which you are seeking legal permanent residence status. For example, refugees and asylees seeking adjustment of status should file Form I-602, Application by Refugee for Waiver of Grounds of Excludability. Individuals seeking adjustment of status based on an approved Form I-130, Petition for Alien Relative, or Form I-140, Immigrant Petition for Alien Worker, are required to file Form I-601, Application for Waiver of Grounds of Inadmissibility.Q. My civil surgeon says that a vaccine is currently t available. What should I do?A. Ask the civil surgeon whether ather health care provider may have the vaccine. If ather physician or department or pharmacy carries the vaccine and can administer the vaccine, you should get the vaccine and request documentation that you have received the vaccine. Bring the written record back to the civil surgeon so that they can complete the Form I-693.HHS/CDC monitors which vaccines are t available in the United States, or which vaccines may experience a shortage. If CDC determines there is a nation-wide shortage of a vaccine, it will recommend to USCIS to post a message on uscis.gov to explain to applicants and civil surgeons whether the vaccine is required and under what circumstances. The information is available on USCIS’ Form I-693 page, the Immigration Medical Examination page, or the Designated Civil Surgeon page.Q. Will USCIS accept a Form I-693 if the vaccination chart is incomplete?A. . The vaccination chart should have at least one entry in each row for each vaccine. If the vaccination chart is t properly completed at the time of the immigration medical examination, USCIS may return the Form I-693 to you with instructions on how to correct it.If you refuse a vaccine because of religious or moral reasons, the civil surgeon will mark this on the Form I-693. In this case, you are inadmissible and will have to apply for a waiver of inadmissibility.Q: Where can I find more information about the vaccination requirements for immigration purposes and how these requirements affect the completion of Form I-693?A. CDC publishes the Technical Instructions for Civil Surgeons, including the vaccination requirements. For more information about the civil surgeon program, the completion of Form I-693, or the adjustment of status application, please visit uscis.gov, or call the USCIS Contact Center at 800-375-5283 (TTY 800-767-1833).Q: Did the CDC’s Vaccination Technical Instructions change for the polio vaccine?A: On May 1, 2024, the Vaccination Technical Instructions for Civil Surgeons changed for the polio vaccine. One dose of IPV should be given to anyone 2 months or older if they are t currently up to date according to ACIP recommendations, including adults who cant show proof of the childhood vaccine series. If the Form I-693 was signed by a civil surgeon on or after May 1, 2024, the new polio vaccine requirement applies.Q: Is the COVID-19 vaccine required for aliens applying for adjustment of status?A. . As of Jan. 20, 2025, aliens applying for adjustment of status are  longer required to provide documentation of having received the COVID-19 vaccination. Therefore, for any adjustment of status application pending on or after January 20, 2025, the alien applying does t need to provide documentation of having completed the COVID-19 vaccination. Prior to Jan. 20, 2025, the COVID-19 vaccine was required based on age. See the chart below for details:COVID-19 Vaccination Requirements Before Jan. 20, 2025Date Civil Surgeon Signed Form I-693Age Required to Receive COVID-19 Vaccination or after Oct. 1, 202112 years of age and olderOn or after v. 3, 20215 years of age and olderOn or after July 25, 20226 months of age and olderRelated LinksVaccination Technical Instructions for Civil Surgeons | CDC Form I-693, Report of Medical Examination and Vaccination RecordCDC: Vaccines and Immunizations42 CFR Part 34.4 Medical tificationsCDC: Guidelines for Vaccinating Pregnant Women Last Reviewed/Updated: 07/08/2025 Vaccination Requirements These Questions and Answers provide basic information about the general vaccination requirements for immigrants (including aliens seeking adjustment of status), and specifically about the assessment made by the civil surgeon to determine whether an alien meets the vaccination requirements. These Questions and Answers do t address the vaccination assessments conducted by panel physicians overseas.For refugees applying for adjustment of status, health department physicians may complete only the vaccination record portion of Form I-693, Report of Medical Examination and Vaccination Record, as blanket-designated civil surgeons.BackgroundUnder the immigration laws of the United States, an alien who applies for an immigrant visa abroad, or who seeks to adjust status to that of a lawful permanent resident while in the United States, is required to receive vaccinations to prevent the following diseases:Mumps;Measles;Rubella;Polio;Tetanus and Diphtheria Toxoids;Pertussis;Haemophilus influenzae type B;Hepatitis B; andAny  vaccine-preventable diseases recommended by the Advisory Committee for Immunization Practices (ACIP). The ACIP is an advisory committee to the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)/Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) that recommends immunizations for the general U.S. population. Since Dec.14, 2009, when the ACIP recommends new vaccines for the general U.S. population, CDC assesses whether these vaccines should be required for immigration purposes on a regular and on an as-needed basis according to specific criteria set by CDC.CDC is responsible for publishing the Technical Instructions for Civil Surgeons. These documents and the HHS regulations set the requirements for the immigration medical examination and are binding on civil surgeons (See the CDC Vaccination Technical Instructions for Civil Surgeons and 42 C.F.R. Section 34.3). The Technical Instructions include a vaccination component, specifying how the civil surgeon has to conduct the vaccination assessment. The civil surgeon records the results of the immigration medical examination, including the results of the vaccination assessment, on USCIS Form I-693.If an alien applies for an immigrant visa abroad, that individual has to undergo an immigration medical examination conducted by a panel physician authorized by the U.S. Department of State (DOS). CDC issues separate instructions to panel physicians designated by DOS to conduct immigration medical examinations abroad. For more information about panel physicians, please consult CDC’s and DOS's websitesTechnical Instructions for Panel Physicians | CDCMedical Examinations FAQs (state.gov).Questions and AnswersQ. If you have an immigration medical examination completed when the flu vaccine is t available to your civil surgeon, then you are t required to document that you have received the seasonal flu vaccine for immigration purposes.Q. Who pays for the vaccinations?A. You are responsible for paying the appropriate fee for all vaccinations. If the civil surgeon is administering the vaccinations, you are responsible for paying the appropriate fee directly to the civil surgeon, as agreed upon with the civil surgeon. You should ask about the price of the vaccinations before the immigration medical examination or the administration of the vaccinations. USCIS does t regulate the fees charged by civil surgeons for the completion of an immigration medical examination. Rates may vary by civil surgeon. It may be helpful to call several local civil surgeons to compare fees. For more information on how to obtain a good faith estimate prior to your appointment, please visit: Understanding costs in advance.Q. Can I be forced to be vaccinated for immigration purposes?A. If you refuse to receive the vaccines required for immigration purposes, as mandated by the immigration laws of the United States, your application for legal permanent resident status may be denied.Q. What will happen if I refuse to receive one or all of the required vaccines?A. Tell the civil surgeon if you do t wish to receive the required vaccines or a particular vaccine. You should also tell the civil surgeon the reason you do t wish to receive the vaccine(s). In this case, a waiver may be available to you, but only under the following circumstances:You are opposed to all vaccinations in any form– a waiver may t be granted if you only object to specific vaccinations;Your objection must be based on religious beliefs or moral convictions; andThe religious or moral beliefs must be sincere.The form used to apply for a waiver depends on the adjustment category under which you are seeking legal permanent residence status. For example, refugees and asylees seeking adjustment of status should file Form I-602, Application by Refugee for Waiver of Grounds of Excludability. Individuals seeking adjustment of status based on an approved Form I-130, Petition for Alien Relative, or Form I-140, Immigrant Petition for Alien Worker, are required to file Form I-601, Application for Waiver of Grounds of Inadmissibility.Q. My civil surgeon says that a vaccine is currently t available. What should I do?A. Ask the civil surgeon whether ather health care provider may have the vaccine. If ather physician or department or pharmacy carries the vaccine and can administer the vaccine, you should get the vaccine and request documentation that you have received the vaccine. Bring the written record back to the civil surgeon so that they can complete the Form I-693.HHS/CDC monitors which vaccines are t available in the United States, or which vaccines may experience a shortage. If CDC determines there is a nation-wide shortage of a vaccine, it will recommend to USCIS to post a message on uscis.gov to explain to applicants and civil surgeons whether the vaccine is required and under what circumstances. The information is available on USCIS’ Form I-693 page, the Immigration Medical Examination page, or the Designated Civil Surgeon page.Q. Will USCIS accept a Form I-693 if the vaccination chart is incomplete?A. . The vaccination chart should have at least one entry in each row for each vaccine. If the vaccination chart is t properly completed at the time of the immigration medical examination, USCIS may return the Form I-693 to you with instructions on how to correct it.If you refuse a vaccine because of religious or moral reasons, the civil surgeon will mark this on the Form I-693. In this case, you are inadmissible and will have to apply for a waiver of inadmissibility.Q: Where can I find more information about the vaccination requirements for immigration purposes and how these requirements affect the completion of Form I-693?A. CDC publishes the Technical Instructions for Civil Surgeons, including the vaccination requirements. For more information about the civil surgeon program, the completion of Form I-693, or the adjustment of status application, please visit uscis.gov, or call the USCIS Contact Center at 800-375-5283 (TTY 800-767-1833).Q: Did the CDC’s Vaccination Technical Instructions change for the polio vaccine?A: On May 1, 2024, the Vaccination Technical Instructions for Civil Surgeons changed for the polio vaccine. One dose of IPV should be given to anyone 2 months or older if they are t currently up to date according to ACIP recommendations, including adults who cant show proof of the childhood vaccine series. If the Form I-693 was signed by a civil surgeon on or after May 1, 2024, the new polio vaccine requirement applies.Q: Is the COVID-19 vaccine required for aliens applying for adjustment of status?A. . As of Jan. 20, 2025, aliens applying for adjustment of status are  longer required to provide documentation of having received the COVID-19 vaccination. Therefore, for any adjustment of status application pending on or after January 20, 2025, the alien applying does t need to provide documentation of having completed the COVID-19 vaccination. Prior to Jan. 20, 2025, the COVID-19 vaccine was required based on age. See the chart below for details:COVID-19 Vaccination Requirements Before Jan. 20, 2025Date Civil Surgeon Signed Form I-693Age Required to Receive COVID-19 Vaccination or after Oct. 1, 202112 years of age and olderOn or after v. 3, 20215 years of age and olderOn or after July 25, 20226 months of age and olderRelated LinksVaccination Technical Instructions for Civil Surgeons | CDC Form I-693, Report of Medical Examination and Vaccination RecordCDC: Vaccines and Immunizations42 CFR Part 34.4 Medical tificationsCDC: Guidelines for Vaccinating Pregnant Women Last Reviewed/Updated: 07/08/2025

Immigration Documents and How to Correct, Update, or Replace Them We issue a variety of secure identity documents that may establish your identity, immigration status in the United States, authorization to work, or authorization to travel. Secure documents include:Arrival-departure records (Form I-94, Form I-94W, or Form I-95);Employment Authorization Documents (Form I-766);Naturalization and citizenship certificates (Form N-550, N-560, N-561, N-570, N-578, or N-645);Permanent Resident Cards, also kwn as Green Cards (Form I-551); andTravel documents (Form I-327, Form I-512, Form I-512L, Form I-512T, or Form I-571)These documents include your personal information, such as your full legal name, date of birth, country of birth, sex, and A-Number.If you are 18 years of age or older, you must always carry your Employment Authorization Document (EAD), Green Card, or  proof of alien registration in the United States with you.You may request replacement of your USCIS-issued secure identity documents if they:Were t delivered;Have expired or will soon expire (renewals);Have been lost, stolen, mutilated, or destroyed; orContain incorrect information.Generally, you need to file a new application form for USCIS to reissue a secure identity document. Depending on the scenario, you may need to pay a new filing fee. Requirements and processes for replacing secure documents vary by document type and the circumstances. Refer to the links below for specific information about replacing your DHS-issued secure documents. See USCIS Policy Manual Volume 11, Part A, Chapter 3, Reissuance of Secure Identity Documents for more information.TE: The information on this page is about DHS-issued immigration documents. Last Reviewed/Updated: 02/18/2025 Immigration Documents and How to Correct, Update, or Replace Them We issue a variety of secure identity documents that may establish your identity, immigration status in the United States, authorization to work, or authorization to travel. Secure documents include:Arrival-departure records (Form I-94, Form I-94W, or Form I-95);Employment Authorization Documents (Form I-766);Naturalization and citizenship certificates (Form N-550, N-560, N-561, N-570, N-578, or N-645);Permanent Resident Cards, also kwn as Green Cards (Form I-551); andTravel documents (Form I-327, Form I-512, Form I-512L, Form I-512T, or Form I-571)These documents include your personal information, such as your full legal name, date of birth, country of birth, sex, and A-Number.If you are 18 years of age or older, you must always carry your Employment Authorization Document (EAD), Green Card, or  proof of alien registration in the United States with you.You may request replacement of your USCIS-issued secure identity documents if they:Were t delivered;Have expired or will soon expire (renewals);Have been lost, stolen, mutilated, or destroyed; orContain incorrect information.Generally, you need to file a new application form for USCIS to reissue a secure identity document. Depending on the scenario, you may need to pay a new filing fee. Requirements and processes for replacing secure documents vary by document type and the circumstances. Refer to the links below for specific information about replacing your DHS-issued secure documents. See USCIS Policy Manual Volume 11, Part A, Chapter 3, Reissuance of Secure Identity Documents for more information.TE: The information on this page is about DHS-issued immigration documents.
